front: The three layers of a Kubernetes platform and their usual tools
back: 1) Cloud + cluster (VPC, EKS/kind, IAM): Terraform. 2) Platform add-ons (gateway controller, cert-manager, Argo CD): Terraform helm provider or GitOps. 3) Applications: GitOps (Argo CD/Flux).

Creating a cluster and configuring the kubernetes/helm providers from its attributes in the same apply: providers get unknown values at plan time, so plans fail (especially `kubernetes_manifest`) or misbehave when the cluster is replaced. Fix: separate stacks.

front: Helm provider v3: provider block syntax
back: `provider "helm" { kubernetes = { host = ..., cluster_ca_certificate = ..., client_certificate = ..., client_key = ... } }` — an attribute with `=`, not a block.
`set = [{ name = "key", value = "val" }]`. Same list style for `set_list` and `set_sensitive`; `registry` blocks became `registries = [...]`.

Typed `*_v1` resources (`kubernetes_deployment_v1`) model core APIs in HCL and only need the API at apply. `kubernetes_manifest` handles any kind incl. CRs via server-side apply but needs the API and CRD at plan time.
Unversioned resources like `kubernetes_deployment` and `kubernetes_namespace` are deprecated; use `kubernetes_deployment_v1`, `kubernetes_namespace_v1`, etc.
Modify an existing cluster. Any change to `kind_config`, name or node image forces destroy and recreate. It also cannot import existing clusters.

front: How do you install a multi-document YAML (e.g. Gateway API CRDs) with Terraform?
back: `for_each` over `provider::kubernetes::manifest_decode_multi(data.http.x.response_body)` into `kubernetes_manifest`, keyed by `"${kind}/${metadata.name}"`. Needs Terraform 1.8+.

front: Why does Helm not upgrade CRDs?
back: Helm installs CRDs from `crds/` only on first install and never upgrades or deletes them (to avoid data loss). Install CRDs separately and before the charts that use them.

front: Where does Terraform end and GitOps begin?
back: Terraform: cloud resources, cluster, minimal platform including Argo CD and a root Application. GitOps: application releases and frequently-changing add-ons. Never let both manage the same object.

front: Why use the `argocd-apps` chart instead of `kubernetes_manifest` for the first Application?
back: Helm renders at apply time, after Argo CD's CRDs exist; `kubernetes_manifest` would need the Application CRD during plan, which fails on a fresh cluster.

Read `aws_eks_cluster` (endpoint, base64 CA → `base64decode`) and use `exec = { api_version = "client.authentication.k8s.io/v1beta1", command = "aws", args = ["eks", "get-token", "--cluster-name", name] }`.
`name` (was `cluster_name`) and `kubernetes_version` (was `cluster_version`), among others. Always read the README of the pinned major.
